title: Use appropriate fetch destination for JSON&CSS modules
body: Fixes https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/7233 - [x] At least two implementers are interested (and none opposed): * Chromium * WebKit - [x] [Tests](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt) are written and can be reviewed and commented upon at: * https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/41665 - [x] [Implementation bugs](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) are filed: * Chromium: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=1491336 * Gecko: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1858078 * WebKit: https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=262946 * Deno: https://github.com/denoland/deno/issues/20866 * Node.js: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/50116 (note: changes to the `Accept` header affect both Node.js and Deno) - [x] [MDN issue](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) is filed: https://github.com/mdn/content/issues/29572 --- I'm working on #7233, to bring the last import-attributes-related pieces to the finishing line. The behavior for CSS modules is easy to define, as it should match how CSS files are loaded in other places: the fetch [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) should be `"style"`, which implies that: - they are fetched with the `Accept: text/css,*/*;q=0.1` header (step 13 of https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch); - they use the `styles-src` CSP instead of `script-src`. ~~On the other hand, I believe there is currently no precedent for loading "generic" (i.e. not something like manifest.json) JSON files, and as such it's less clear what the behavior should be. This PR sets the destination to `""` and hard-codes the `Accept: application/json,*/*;q=0.5` header **(*)**, and as a consequence:~~ https://github.com/whatwg/fetch/pull/1691 introduces `"json"` destination in fetch, so that: - JSON modules are fetches with the `Accept: application/json,*/*;q=0.5` header (the `*/*` has a `q` value higher than for CSS modules because there are actually [many valid JSON mime types](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#json-mime-type), but we cannot cover them with a glob pattern because it's not possible to indicate "it must end with `+json`") - they use the `connect-src` CSP policy instead of `script-src` (https://github.com/w3c/webappsec-csp/pull/611), similar to JSON loaded using `fetch`. ~~**(*)** the list of valid JSON mime types is potentially unbounded, since it includes any mime type that ends in `+json` (ref: [JSON mime types](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#json-mime-type)). This `Accept:` is currently hard-coded in HTML, but maybe it should be moved to Fetch by defining a new `"json"` fetch destination.~~ ~~Additionally, I need some clarification on the `mode` of requests for modules coming from workers&friends (related: https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/3656). The current logic sets the request's mode to same-origin if the destination is worker/sharedworker/serviceworker. This PR changes the destination for CSS/JSON modules, and I'm not sure if it should also affect the request mode or not.~~ (Answer: no - https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/9486#issuecomment-1631877548) TODO (other specs): - [x] Update the list of ways to fetch stylesheets at https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#directive-style-src - [x] Maybe add the features list of https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#destination-table to mention JSON modules - [ ] ~~Does this change have implications for [https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#should-response-to-request-be-blocked-due-to-nosniff?](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#should-response-to-request-be-blocked-due-to-nosniff?)?~~ (Answer: no - https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/9486#issuecomment-1631877548) *** /links.html ( diff ) /webappapis.html ( diff )
